messages.author: 5e649bb0b1e892e9
messages.subject: Recomputation after adding further CEL-files
parts:
Dear Henrik

I run the following commands with e.g. 10 CEL-files:
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs);
csAcc <- process(acc, verbose=verbose);
qua <- QuantileNormalization(csAcc);
csQua <- process(qua, verbose=verbose);
plm <- RmaCnPlm(csQua, mergeStrands=TRUE,
combineAlleles=TRUE, ...);
fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces);
cesFln <- process(fln, verbose=verbose);
model <- GladModel(cesFln, NULL);
ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(model);
tmp <- process(ce, arrays=arrays, chromosomes=chromosomes,
force=F);

As you see, I normalize the data first, including quantile
normalization.

My question is, what happens when I add e.g. further 4 CEL-files
resulting in 14 CEL-files, and re-run the analysis:
Does aroma correctly recognize the 14 CEL-files and re-run the
normalization (including quantile) and re-run GLAD afterwards, or do I
need to force certain methods? If so, which methods need "force=T"?

Best regards
Christian

<Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:

> Dear Henrik
>
> I run the following commands with e.g. 10 CEL-files:
> acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs);
> csAcc <- process(acc, verbose=verbose);
> qua <- QuantileNormalization(csAcc);
> csQua <- process(qua, verbose=verbose);
> plm <- RmaCnPlm(csQua, mergeStrands=TRUE,
> combineAlleles=TRUE, ...);
> fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
> ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);
> fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces);
> cesFln <- process(fln, verbose=verbose);
> model <- GladModel(cesFln, NULL);
> ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(model);
> tmp <- process(ce, arrays=arrays, chromosomes=chromosomes,
> force=F);
>
> As you see, I normalize the data first, including quantile
> normalization.
>
> My question is, what happens when I add e.g. further 4 CEL-files
> resulting in 14 CEL-files, and re-run the analysis:
> Does aroma correctly recognize the 14 CEL-files and re-run the
> normalization (including quantile) and re-run GLAD afterwards, or do I
> need to force certain methods? If so, which methods need "force=T"?

There is no support for detecting and handling additions/modifications
of input data sets [although I had it in mind while developing so one
day it might be possible to add what is missing]. So, you have to
handle this manually, which is easiest to do by deleting the
directories to be redone. You don't have to do this for
AllelicCrosstalkCalibration though (unless you've done something
different before in the pipeline).

TECHNICAL DETAILS:
Basically all calibration and normalization methods will check if the
output/result file exists, and if it does it will skip it. Note that
this does not do what you want for QuantileNormalization, because the
normalized data is a function of the input CEL file and the target
distribution, which is a function of all CEL files. In other words,
when you add a new array, the target distribution will be different,
but already normalized arrays will not be normalized and therefore not
be a function of this new target distribution. If you specify you own
'targetDistribution', then this will not be a problem and
QuantileNormalization basically becomes a single-array normalization
method. FragmentLengthNormalization is of the same nature as
QuantileNormalization.
Summary: You have to redo QuantileNormalization and
FragmentLengthNormalization for the complete data set. The easiest is
to just delete the directory (I haven't validated that force=TRUE will
"force" itself recursively through all parts - it should though).

AllelicCrosstalkCalibration is quite special because it is a
single-array method, so it will actual support addition of new arrays.
For example, if you add an array the AllelicCrosstalkCalibration will
not find it and will indeed calibrate it. However, if you modify an
input file, that is, have the same CEL file name but with different
data [can happen in rare cases], the AllelicCrosstalkCalibration will
*not* detect that.
Summary: You don't have to redo AllelicCrosstalkCalibration for old arrays.

Probe-level summarization based on multi-array models, e.g.
log-additive (RmaPlm), fits the parameters based on all arrays. The
way aroma.affymetrix detects if a PLM for a particular unit is fitted
or not is by looking at the very last array in the data set and see if
the chip effects for that unit is positive or not (zero or below means
not fitted). Arrays are always ordered in lexicographic order
according to their filenames. Thus, the last array is the one that
comes last in lexicographic sense. So, if you add an array that has a
filename so it becomes last in this sense, aroma.affymetrix will look
for *its* chip effects to decide if the PLM is fitted or not, and
conclude for every unit that is *not* - all units will be refitted.
However, if you add arrays but "the last" array remains the same,
aroma.affymetrix will not refit the model - your new arrays will all
have zero parameter estimates.
Summary: You have to redo RmaPlm for the complete data set. The
easiest is to just delete the directory (but force=TRUE should do).

The GladModel and friends are single-array single-chromosome models.
However, the old estimates will of course be incorrect due to the
above, so you have to refit everything.
Summary: You have to redo the GladModel for the complete data set.
The easiest is to just delete the directory (but force=TRUE should
do).

Hope this helps

Henrik

>
> Best regards
> Christian
